title: Unsupervised Alignment of Hypergraphs with Different Scales

problem.claim: Identify correspondences between people represented as nodes in two hypergraphs using information about their group memberships across platforms.

gap.claim: The two hypergraphs may have hyperedge sets with significantly different scales because people use different applications at different time periods.

narrative_sequence.summary: People interact in groups, and those groups may occur across different platforms such as messaging applications.
The task is to identify the same people across platforms from group information, formalized as finding node correspondences between two hypergraphs.
Nodes represent people and hyperedges represent groups of people.
The hyperedge sets can differ substantially in scale because platform use changes across time.

source_observation.claim: Group interactions can provide information for matching people across platforms.

interpretation.claim: Relational structure may support cross-platform entity alignment when direct identity information is unavailable.

application.claim: Represent people as nodes and groups as hyperedges when applying structural alignment to multi-person interactions.

exception.claim: Alignment methods should account for substantial differences in hyperedge scale across platforms or time periods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the alignment method.
The abstract does not report experiments, datasets, metrics, or results.
